tables.caption: Trip Customs Overview
rows: Japan exit + airline security; US customs on US arrival

tables.caption: Immigration
rows: Not required — US passport, tourism ≤90 days (03-immigration-entry)
Passport, return/onward ticket, first-night hotel address
Visit Japan Web QR for immigration + customs (complete within 72 hr of departure)
30–60 min typical at NRT; often faster at HND

tables.caption: Duty-free allowances (bringing goods into Japan)
rows: Up to 3 bottles (760 ml each) if ≥20 years old
400 cigarettes, or 100 cigars, or 500 g tobacco
Total value generally ≤ ¥200,000 for personal use without duty (verify current Japan Customs notice)

tables.caption: Prohibited / restricted (high-signal)
rows: Zero tolerance; includes some US OTC (e.g. pseudoephedrine in cold meds)
Restricted—do not bring from US; declare or discard

tables.caption: Within Japan (Domestic)
rows: None between Tokyo, Takayama, Kyoto, Osaka
Carry passport or photocopy—some hotels require passport at check-in
See below; not a border crossing but affects departure
Open food items consumed in Japan OK; do not pack fresh food for US return

tables.caption: Tax-Free Shopping (Japan)
rows: Tourists on short stay; passport required at purchase
Consumption tax 10% waived on eligible goods
Stores displaying Tax-Free sign (department stores, electronics, some drugstores)
Show passport; goods sealed in bag until departure from Japan
If asked, present purchases + receipts at customs inspection before check-in (usually quick for compliant sealed bags)

bullets.heading: US Re-Entry Customs (Final Leg Home)
items: Food: Generally no fresh fruit, meat, rice, or agricultural products—packaged commercial tea/candy often allowed; when unsure, declare.
Gifts for others — count toward your $800.
